newsitem.title: JAPAN: Stasco begins Oman crude talks with Asia customers.
newsitem.headline: Stasco begins Oman crude talks with Asia customers.

text.p: Shell International Trading and Shipping Co (Stasco) said on Thursday that it had started to meet Asian customers to discuss the price for Oman crude oil for lifting in 1997.
"(Stasco officials) are meeting South Korea traders (this week)...and planning to meet Japanese traders next week," a Stasco official in Tokyo said.
Officials from London were meeting South Korean traders, while officials based in Tokyo would be talking to customers here, he said.
"We are mainly listening at this stage to find out points of view," a second Stasco crude source said.
The Oman crude oil term price for 1997 will probably be set by mid-November, but the Tokyo official declined to comment on what the price was likely to be.

The 1996 Oman crude oil term price for Stasco's Asian customers was set at MPM plus eight cents, two cents down from the 1995 price. In 1996, Oman has consistently traded on the spot market at around 10 cents over MPM.
Tokyo traders said the 1997 price was likely to be higher than that for 1996 given this year's strong crude oil market.
Fundamentals appear to be lined up on the bullish side.
"I think it will be 10 (cents) or a little bit higher... I do believe it won't be less than 10 (cents)," one trader said.
Oman's official crude oil price for September was $21.20, its highest level so far this year and up from its year low of $16.50 for liftings in February.

Tightening product specifications are leading to growing demand for lighter crudes, with strong demand for Far East light sweet grades. Once that supply is taken, demand is passed on to the next line of crudes, like Oman.
